$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-6(s-1)}{s(s-3)}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-3=2{X}_{1}(s)-{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+6=-2{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-2){X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)=3 \\ 2{X}_{1}(s)+(s-1){X}_{2}(s)=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{-6-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-2)[\frac{-6-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2}]+{X}_{2}(s) & =3 \\ (s-2)[-6-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)]+2{X}_{2}(s) & =6 \\ -6(s-2)-(s-2)(s-1){X}_{2}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s) & =6 \\ [-(s-2)(s-1)+2]{X}_{2}(s) & =6+6(s-2) \\ (-{s}^{2}+3s){X}_{2}(s) & =6s-6 \\ -s(s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =6(s-1) \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-6(s-1)}{s(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-6-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6-(s-1)(\frac{-6(s-1)}{s(s-3)})}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6+\frac{6(s-1)^{2}}{s(s-3)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6s(s-3)+6(s-1)^{2}}{2s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{3(s+1)}{s(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3(s+1)}{s(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-6(s-1)}{s(s-3)}.
$$
